title: Trust in God Alone
overview: Psalm 62 is a profound declaration of unwavering trust in God as the sole source of salvation, strength, and refuge. Attributed to David and directed to the chief musician Jeduthun, this psalm emphasizes the futility of human schemes and the emptiness of worldly power and riches. It calls believers to patiently wait on God, pour out their hearts before Him, and reject reliance on oppression or wealth. The psalm highlights God's justice and mercy, affirming that ultimate power belongs to Him and that He rewards each person according to their deeds. This chapter stands as a timeless exhortation to place complete confidence in God amidst adversity and deceit, reinforcing key biblical themes of faith, divine protection, and righteous judgment.
structure:
**Verses 1-2: Expression of Trust and Confidence.** The psalm opens with David’s personal testimony of waiting on God alone for salvation and defense, establishing God as his unshakable rock.

**Verses 3-4: The Reality of Opposition.** David addresses the malicious intentions of his enemies who seek to undermine him through lies and deceit, highlighting the instability of those who oppose God’s anointed.

**Verses 5-7: Reaffirmation of Faith.** The psalmist commands his own soul to wait quietly on God, reiterating God’s role as rock, salvation, and refuge, reinforcing the theme of steadfast trust.

**Verses 8-10: Call to Trust and Warning Against Worldly Confidence.** A communal exhortation invites all people to trust God continually, to pour out their hearts before Him, and warns against placing confidence in oppression or riches.

**Verses 11-12: Divine Sovereignty and Justice.** The psalm concludes with a solemn declaration that power belongs to God alone and that He mercifully recompenses each person according to their works, underscoring God’s righteous judgment.

keyVerses.text: He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
keyVerses.significance: This verse encapsulates the psalmist’s absolute confidence in God as the unshakeable foundation and protector, highlighting the theological truth that God alone is the source of true security and salvation.

keyVerses.text: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
keyVerses.significance: This verse serves as a universal call to persistent trust and honest prayer, emphasizing God’s role as a refuge for all believers, which is central to the psalm’s message of faith and dependence on God.

keyVerses.text: God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God.
keyVerses.significance: This declaration affirms God’s ultimate sovereignty and authority over all things, reminding believers that human power is subordinate to divine power, a key theological foundation of trust in God.

keyVerses.text: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights God’s merciful nature alongside His justice, affirming the biblical principle of divine recompense and encouraging righteous living grounded in accountability before God.

characters.name: David
characters.description: The psalmist and king of Israel, David is the speaker who expresses deep personal trust in God amidst opposition. His role is to model faith and reliance on God’s protection and justice.

characters.name: God
characters.description: Portrayed as the only true rock, salvation, defense, and refuge, God is the central figure of trust and power in the psalm. He is sovereign, merciful, and just, rewarding each person according to their deeds.

characters.name: Enemies/Opponents
characters.description: These unnamed adversaries plot mischief against the psalmist, delighting in lies and hypocrisy. They symbolize the instability and futility of opposing God’s purposes.

themes.description: The psalm consistently exhorts believers to place unwavering trust in God alone as their rock and salvation, rejecting reliance on human strength or wealth. This theme aligns with the broader biblical call to faith in God’s providence.
Psalm 62 emphasizes that all power belongs to God and that He will render to each according to their works, reflecting the biblical doctrine of divine sovereignty and righteous judgment.
The psalm contrasts the stability of God with the instability of human plans and deceit, warning against trusting in oppression, riches, or falsehoods, consistent with biblical wisdom literature.

themes.theme: Prayer and Pouring Out the Heart
themes.description: Believers are encouraged to pour out their hearts before God continually, highlighting the importance of honest, persistent prayer as a means of expressing trust and dependence.

historicalContext: Psalm 62 is attributed to King David, who reigned over Israel approximately 1000 BC. The psalm reflects a period of political instability and personal opposition, common in David’s life, where enemies sought to undermine his rule. The reference to Jeduthun, a chief musician, indicates the psalm’s use in temple worship, emphasizing its liturgical function. The cultural context includes a society where kingship was divinely appointed, and trust in God as protector was essential for survival and legitimacy. The political environment was marked by internal strife and external threats, making the themes of refuge and divine justice particularly poignant.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God’s absolute sovereignty and the believer’s sole dependence on Him for salvation and strength, seeing Psalm 62 as a call to faith that rejects all human confidence and trusts in God’s providential care.

Dispensational interpreters often see this psalm as reflecting God’s protective care for His anointed king, foreshadowing Christ as the ultimate Rock and Savior, with the enemies representing worldly opposition to God’s kingdom.

Early Church Fathers interpreted Psalm 62 allegorically, viewing the rock and salvation as Christ Himself, encouraging believers to place their hope in Him alone amidst spiritual trials and opposition.

This verse complements Psalm 62’s theme of God’s sovereign control and care for those who trust Him.

application: Place your full trust in God as your unshakable rock and refuge, especially in times of trial.
Resist the temptation to rely on wealth, power, or human schemes for security.
Practice honest and continual prayer by pouring out your heart before God.
Remember that God is sovereign and will justly reward each person according to their deeds.
Encourage others to trust God at all times, fostering a community grounded in faith.
Wait patiently and quietly on God’s timing, confident in His salvation and defense.
conclusion: Psalm 62 remains a powerful reminder for believers to anchor their faith exclusively in God’s steadfast character. It challenges Christians to reject worldly confidence and instead embrace patient trust, honest prayer, and reliance on God’s sovereign justice and mercy. Through its vivid imagery of God as rock, refuge, and salvation, the psalm calls the church to unwavering faith amid opposition and uncertainty, assuring that God’s power and recompense are sure. This timeless message continues to inspire believers to live with courage and hope grounded in the Lord alone.
timeline: c. 1000 BC - Reign of King David in Israel

outline.heading: Expression of Personal Trust in God
outline.description: David begins by declaring his soul’s waiting upon God alone, affirming God as his rock, salvation, and defense, establishing the foundation of trust.

outline.heading: Confrontation with Enemies’ Deceit
outline.description: The psalmist describes the malicious intentions and hypocrisy of his adversaries, emphasizing their instability and ultimate downfall.

outline.heading: Renewed Call to Quiet Waiting and Confidence
outline.description: David commands his soul to wait quietly on God, restating God’s role as rock and refuge, reinforcing steadfast faith.

outline.heading: Exhortation to Trust and Pour Out Hearts
outline.description: A communal appeal encourages continual trust in God, open prayer, and warns against placing confidence in oppression or riches.

outline.heading: Declaration of God’s Sovereignty and Justice
outline.description: The psalm concludes with the affirmation that power belongs to God and that He mercifully rewards each according to their works.
